seo.title: Homeless help in Manchester - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Manchester: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Manchester homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Nowhere safe to stay tonight: Manchester City Council 0161 234 5001, 24 hours for genuine emergencies Housing assessment and advice, weekdays 9am–4:30pm: 0161 234 4692 Sleeping outside, weekdays 9am–4:30pm: council outreach 0161 234 5339; out of hours 0161 234 5001 Urgent but not life-threatening medical or mental-health help: NHS 111; select option 2 for urgent mental-health support
page.notice: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, alert or referral does not guarantee accommodation. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.
Start here: call the council if you have nowhere safe tonight. If you are sleeping outside, also contact the outreach team or make a StreetLink alert with your exact location. If you may lose your home within 56 days, ask the council for homelessness prevention help now.
page.footer: Is something wrong or outdated? Submit a correction. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
NHS guidance on calling 999

entries.title: Manchester City Council: nowhere safe tonight
entries.description:
Emergency-only phone: 0161 234 5001, 24 hours. Use it when there is an immediate threat to health or safety and you have nowhere to stay at night.
Daytime housing assessment and advice: 0161 234 4692, Monday–Friday 9am–4:30pm. Say clearly that you want to make a homeless application and whether you need emergency accommodation that day.
The council must assess the circumstances; temporary accommodation depends on the law and the assessment. Explain pregnancy, children, disability, illness, violence, care history or another reason you may be especially vulnerable.
Council emergency contacts

entries.title: Council prevention help: at risk within 56 days
entries.description:
Ask for help as soon as you may lose your home. Take an eviction notice, tenancy papers, messages from the person asking you to leave and identity or income records if you have them, but contact the council even when documents are missing.
An online referral is not the route for a same-day emergency. Call the numbers above when you cannot stay safely tonight.
Council homelessness prevention and advice

entries.title: Manchester rough-sleeping outreach team
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 234 5339, Monday–Friday 9am–4:30pm. Outside these hours: 0161 234 5001.
Give a precise sleeping location, usual time and identifying description. The team works within Manchester city boundaries and cannot guarantee that it will find someone or provide a bed on the first contact.
Report someone sleeping rough

entries.title: StreetLink
entries.description:
Make an alert or self-referral for a person sleeping outside. Include the exact public location and when the person is usually there. StreetLink is not an emergency service and does not itself provide accommodation.
Make a StreetLink alert or self-referral

entries.title: A Bed Every Night and severe-weather provision
entries.description:
Manchester participates in A Bed Every Night and activates extra severe-weather arrangements. Access is normally through the council, outreach or a partner assessment, not by arriving at a building without referral.
Ask whether provision is active and whether a referral is appropriate. A referral is not a promise of a bed, and the location may change.
Council rough-sleeping programmes

categories.title: Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

entries.title: Barnabus: The Beacon
entries.description:
Phone: 07507 794077. Beacon drop-in: Monday–Thursday 9am–12 noon. The support office is normally open Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm.
For adults aged 18+. Food and essentials, clothing, showers, NHS nurses, housing and benefits help, mental-health and substance-use support, employment help and activities. Barnabus is a Christian charity; help is based on need.
Barnabus | current partnership listing — https://mhp.org.uk/support-organisation/barnabus/
entries.address: Address: 45 Bloom Street, Manchester M1 3LY

entries.title: Booth Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 835 2499; email: info@boothcentre.org.uk. Usually open Monday–Friday 8am–4pm; check the day's programme. — mailto:info@boothcentre.org.uk
Breakfast café, lunch, wellbeing and skills activities, and help with housing, income and employment. Visiting services and activities may have separate times.
Booth Centre get-help information
entries.address: Address: Edward Holt House, Pimblett Street, Manchester M3 1FU

entries.title: Caritas Cornerstone Day Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 232 8888; email: Cornerstone@caritassalford.org.uk. Open Monday–Friday 9:30am–1pm. — mailto:Cornerstone@caritassalford.org.uk
Housing and benefits advice, energy, health, substance-use, mental-health and immigration help; showers; activities; an optician; and lunch and warm space from 12 noon–1pm. No general referral is required, but advice slots vary.
Cornerstone is run by the Catholic charity Caritas Diocese of Salford and supports people of any or no faith.
Caritas Cornerstone
entries.address: Address: 104B Denmark Road, Hulme, Manchester M15 6JS

entries.title: Coffee4Craig
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 383 2926; email: office@coffee4craig.co.uk. — mailto:office@coffee4craig.co.uk
Public drop-in: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 6pm–8pm; Sunday 5pm–7pm. Thursday and Saturday are closed. Some afternoon sessions are invitation-only.
Hot meals, showers, clothing, advice and referrals for adults aged 18+, with priority for people sleeping outside. The showers are upstairs and there is no lift.
current Coffee4Craig listing
entries.address: Address: The Meanwhile, Unit 5, 153 Great Ducie Street, Manchester M3 1FB

entries.title: Lifeshare
entries.description:
Office and drop-in: 1st Floor, 36–38 Sackville Street, Manchester M1 3WA; phone 07375 510222.
Lifeshare breakfast service
entries.address: Breakfast address: Mosaic Wellbeing Hub, 2 Dale Street, Manchester M1 1JW
entries.hours: Breakfast: Friday, Saturday and Sunday 7am–9am. Free breakfast, hot drinks, dry clothes, showers and takeaway food are normally available.

entries.title: Mustard Tree
entries.description:
Help desk: 0161 850 2282. General and referrals: 0161 228 7331; email: referrals@mustardtree.org.uk. — mailto:referrals@mustardtree.org.uk
Registration is required; bring photo ID and benefit evidence if available, or explain what is missing. Services include a Food Club, low-cost community shop, training, groups and help with furniture after rehousing.
A multi-agency Street Engagement Hub is normally held Tuesday and Thursday 10am–1pm. Partner attendance changes.
Mustard Tree get-help information
entries.address: Address: 110 Oldham Road, Ancoats, Manchester M4 6AG

entries.title: Caritas Morning Star supported accommodation
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 868 0606; email: morningstar@caritassalford.org.uk. — mailto:morningstar@caritassalford.org.uk
Supported accommodation for single homeless men. It is not a walk-in shelter and does not accept self-referrals: contact Manchester City Council first.
Morning Star access information
entries.address: Address: 104 Denmark Road, Manchester M15 6JS

entries.title: Centrepoint Manchester: young adults
entries.description:
Manchester accommodation is for people aged 18–25 referred after a council housing assessment. It is not a walk-in shelter. National youth housing helpline, ages 16–25: 0808 800 0661, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm.
Centrepoint Manchester | Centrepoint Helpline — https://centrepoint.org.uk/contact-help
entries.address: Address: 52 Oldham Street, Manchester M4 1LE

entries.title: Street Support Manchester directory
entries.description:
Use the live directory to find nearby meals, health care, practical help and accommodation advice. Filter by need and check the provider's current details before setting out.
Street Support Manchester

entries.title: Barnabus
entries.description:
Food and essential items are normally available Monday–Thursday 9am–12 noon alongside showers, clothing and casework.
Barnabus current listing

entries.title: Booth Centre café
entries.description:
Weekday breakfast and lunch are offered with housing, employment and income support. Call 0161 835 2499 to confirm the day's times.
Booth Centre

entries.title: Caritas Cornerstone community lunch
entries.description:
Free community lunch and warm space Monday–Friday 12 noon–1pm at 104B Denmark Road, M15 6JS.
Cornerstone

entries.title: Coffee4Craig evening meals
entries.description:
Hot meals during public drop-in Monday–Wednesday and Friday 6pm–8pm, and Sunday 5pm–7pm, at 153 Great Ducie Street, M3 1FB. Closed Thursday and Saturday.
current timetable

entries.title: Lifeshare weekend breakfast
entries.description:
Free breakfast and hot drinks Friday–Sunday 7am–9am at 2 Dale Street, M1 1JW, with showers and dry clothes subject to capacity.
Lifeshare breakfast

entries.title: Audacious Church A-Teams
entries.description:
A Christian outreach team provides hot food and support on Tuesday evenings and Thursday mornings. The official page does not publish fixed public times, so confirm before travelling.
Email: julianwolstencroft@audaciouschurch.com. — mailto:julianwolstencroft@audaciouschurch.com
Audacious A-Teams
entries.address: Address: Audacious Church, Trinity Way, Manchester M3 7BD

entries.title: Manchester Central Foodbank
entries.description:
Phone: 07928 412339; email: info@manchestercentral.foodbank.org.uk. A voucher or partner referral is normally required. — mailto:info@manchestercentral.foodbank.org.uk
- Openshaw: St Clement's Church, Ashton Old Road, M11 1HF; Tuesday 2pm–4pm.
- Harpurhey: Harpurhey Neighbourhood Project, Carisbrook Street, M9 5PR; Thursday 10:30am–12:30pm.
- Ardwick: Brunswick Parish Church, Brunswick Street, M13 9SX; Friday 10:30am–12:30pm.
Do not travel to the Trinity Methodist Church admin address for food: it is not a distribution centre. Confirm the voucher and session.
Foodbank locations and access rules

entries.title: Mustard Tree Food Club
entries.description:
Registered clients can use the Food Club and low-cost shop. This is not an immediate free meal; membership, eligibility and payment may apply.
Mustard Tree access

entries.title: FoodCycle Salford Cornerstone: nearby no-referral meal
entries.description:
Free vegetarian community meal Tuesday at 6:15pm, no booking required. This is in Salford, outside Manchester city.
FoodCycle Salford
entries.address: Address: 451 Liverpool Street, Salford M6 5QQ

entries.title: Council food-help finders
entries.description:
Find referral foodbanks and services available without a referral. Contact the provider because stock, times and voucher rules change.
Manchester food support

entries.title: Barnabus
entries.description:
Showers, clothing and essentials are available during the Monday–Thursday morning drop-in, subject to capacity and supplies.
Barnabus listing

entries.title: Caritas Cornerstone
entries.description:
Showers are normally available Monday–Friday 9:30am–1pm. Ask about toiletries and clothing.
Cornerstone services

entries.title: Coffee4Craig
entries.description:
Showers and clothing are available during public evening drop-ins, subject to demand. Showers are upstairs and there is no lift.
Coffee4Craig practical help

entries.title: Lifeshare
entries.description:
Showers and dry clothes are available during Friday–Sunday breakfast, 7am–9am, subject to capacity.
Lifeshare facilities

entries.title: Laundry and replacement clothing
entries.description:
Public laundry access is limited. Ask Barnabus, Booth Centre, Cornerstone, Coffee4Craig, Lifeshare or an accommodation worker which current partner can wash clothes or issue replacements.
Search practical support

entries.title: Urban Village Medical Practice Homeless Health Service
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 272 5656. Specialist primary care for people experiencing homelessness in Manchester.
Weekday GP clinics are published for 9am–12 noon and 2pm–5pm. Registration drop-in is Thursday 10am–12 noon; wound-dressing drop-ins are normally Monday, Wednesday and Friday 2pm–4pm. Call first because schedules change.
Homeless Health Service clinics
entries.address: Address: Ancoats Primary Care Centre, Old Mill Street, Manchester M4 6EE

entries.title: Register with an NHS GP without an address or ID
entries.description:
You do not need proof of address, immigration status, identification or an NHS number to register. A practice should not refuse solely because these are missing. You may give a temporary address, the surgery address or no fixed address.
NHS GP registration rules

entries.title: Barnabus and Cornerstone health services
entries.description:
Barnabus has NHS nursing support and Cornerstone hosts health services including an optician. Ask for the next clinic.
Barnabus | Cornerstone — https://mhp.org.uk/support-organisation/barnabus/

entries.title: Urgent NHS care
entries.description:
Call 111 or use NHS 111 online for urgent problems that are not life-threatening. Call 999 for a life-threatening emergency.
NHS 111 online

entries.title: Dental care
entries.description:
Use the NHS dentist finder. For urgent dental pain, swelling, bleeding or trauma, call NHS 111.
Find an NHS dentist

entries.title: Help with health costs
entries.description:
Some benefits qualify automatically; others can apply through the NHS Low Income Scheme. Homelessness alone does not make prescriptions free.
NHS Low Income Scheme

entries.title: Urgent mental-health support: NHS 111 option 2
entries.description:
Call 111 and select mental-health option 2. It is free, available 24 hours and can be used for yourself or someone else of any age.
Important: the former Greater Manchester 0800 crisis number closed on 3 November 2025. Call 999 or go to A&E if there is an immediate risk to life.
Greater Manchester urgent mental-health support

entries.title: No.93 Crisis Café, Harpurhey
entries.description:
Phone ahead: 0161 271 0339 or 07778 012838. Monday–Friday 8pm–1am; Saturday–Sunday 3pm–1am.
Supportive out-of-hours space for mental-health crisis. It is not an emergency department or accommodation service.
No.93 Crisis Café
entries.address: Address: 93 Church Lane, Manchester M9 5BG

entries.title: Samaritans
entries.description:
Call 116 123, free, 24 hours, for confidential listening. Call 999 in immediate danger.
Contact Samaritans

entries.title: Shout
entries.description:
Text SHOUT to 85258 for free confidential crisis-text support in the UK.
Shout support

entries.title: Change Grow Live: Manchester drug and alcohol service
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 823 6306; email: Manchester@cgl.org.uk. Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, with some later hub appointments. — mailto:Manchester@cgl.org.uk
Adults can self-refer for harm reduction, needle exchange, recovery support, prescribing, detox or rehabilitation assessment, testing, housing and employment help.
Manchester drug and alcohol service

entries.title: Drug or alcohol emergency
entries.description:
Call 999 for unconsciousness, seizures, blue or grey lips, severe breathing problems or suspected overdose. Stay with the person and follow instructions.
NHS poisoning guidance

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: Central Library
entries.description:
Open Monday–Thursday 9am–8pm and Friday–Saturday 9am–5pm. Libraries provide free Wi-Fi and warm public space. Free membership gives access to public computers, normally for up to two hours.
Library opening times | Wi-Fi and computers — https://www.manchester.gov.uk/libraries/use-wifi-or-a-library-computer
entries.address: Address: St Peter's Square, Manchester M2 5PD

entries.title: Free public toilets
entries.description:
The council lists free accessible toilets at the Town Hall Extension, Central Library, Manchester Arndale, Piccadilly Station and Victoria Station. At Victoria, ask the Duty Manager for the accessible-toilet key.
Manchester public-toilet list

entries.title: Warm Welcome spaces
entries.description:
Libraries and participating venues provide free warm space, seating, Wi-Fi and information. The 2026 campaign lists self-service hot drinks from 19 October 2026 to February 2027; supplies and venue hours vary.
Warm Welcome spaces 2026–27

entries.title: Digital access help
entries.description:
Text 07860 064128 or email digitalinclusion@manchester.gov.uk for help getting online. — sms:+447860064128 — mailto:digitalinclusion@manchester.gov.uk
Council digital access information

entries.title: Bee Network journey planning
entries.description:
Use the official planner for buses, trams and trains. Ask a housing, health or Jobcentre worker whether appointment travel can be authorised; help is not automatic.
Bee Network journey planner

entries.title: Travel to a new job
entries.description:
The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help an eligible resident with travel when starting a job. Apply before buying a long-term ticket when possible.
Crisis and Resilience Fund

entries.title: Manchester Airport by train
entries.description:
Trains from Piccadilly normally take about 20 minutes and run frequently. The airport station is a covered 5–15 minute walk from terminals. Check live times and prices.
Airport train information

entries.title: Manchester Airport by tram
entries.description:
Trams connect the airport with Manchester Victoria, normally about every 12 minutes. Buy a ticket or touch in before boarding and check the Bee Network on the day.
If stranded at the airport, speak to airport staff or police. The terminal is not accommodation; call the council emergency number if you have nowhere safe.
Airport tram information

entries.title: Manchester Cost of Living Advice Line
entries.description:
Freephone: 0800 023 2692, Monday–Friday 9am–4:30pm.
Ask about benefits and rent, debt and bills, food, internet, laptops, phones or data. Translation and SignVideo access are available. The line gives advice and referrals; it cannot guarantee a grant.
Cost of Living Advice Line

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim Universal Credit when homeless. With permission, use a trusted person's address, a hostel or day-centre address, or the Jobcentre address. DWP should offer help if you lack ID, internet, email, a bank account or a National Insurance number.
Ask Barnabus, Booth Centre, Cornerstone, Mustard Tree or Citizens Advice before using any organisation's address.
Official Universal Credit guidance for homeless people

entries.title: Manchester Crisis and Resilience Fund
entries.description:
Manchester residents on a low income who face a sudden crisis and cannot afford essentials may be able to get short-term help with food, energy, household items or travel to a new job. Each application is assessed and help is not guaranteed.
Crisis and Resilience Fund options

entries.title: Council cash grant
entries.description:
Eligible Manchester residents aged 16+ with no savings and certain means-tested benefits can apply for a £30 or £60 emergency grant. The crisis must be outside their control, and a previous grant within 12 months usually prevents another award.
Approval is not automatic and the scheme does not replace broken furniture or white goods.
Cash-grant eligibility and application

entries.title: Housing Payments for a rent shortfall
entries.description:
From April 2026, Manchester Housing Payments replaced Discretionary Housing Payments. You may apply if you receive Housing Benefit or the Universal Credit housing-cost element and live in Manchester, or the council placed you outside Manchester.
Payments are not guaranteed. For a paper form or help call 0161 234 5678, Monday–Friday 9am–4:30pm.
Manchester Housing Payments

entries.title: Housing Benefit in supported accommodation
entries.description:
Housing Benefit can still apply in some supported, sheltered or temporary accommodation. Ask the provider and council which claim is correct.
GOV.UK Housing Benefit guidance

categories.title: Work, training and travel to a new job

entries.title: Booth Centre employment support
entries.description:
Ask about one-to-one employment and income help, skills activities, volunteering and current visiting agencies.
Booth Centre

entries.title: Caritas Cornerstone Work Club
entries.description:
Normally Wednesday and Friday 9:30am–1pm without an appointment. Help includes CVs, job applications and digital skills. Confirm before travelling.
Council Work Club listing
entries.address: Address: 104B Denmark Road, Manchester M15 6JS

entries.title: Mustard Tree Freedom Project
entries.description:
Structured training, qualifications, work experience and support, normally two days a week for four to six months. Registration and suitability rules apply.
Mustard Tree training

entries.title: Back on Track Manchester
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 834 1661; email: info@backontrackmanchester.org.uk. — mailto:info@backontrackmanchester.org.uk
Training, employability, wellbeing and practical courses for adults who have experienced homelessness, mental ill health, recovery or the criminal-justice system. Ask for the current programme and referral route.
Back on Track contact
entries.address: Address: 4th Floor, Swan Buildings, 20 Swan Street, Manchester M4 5JW

entries.title: Find vacancies and a Jobcentre
entries.description:
Use GOV.UK Find a Job and the official Jobcentre finder. Libraries and day centres can help with computer access.
Find a Job | find a Jobcentre — https://find-your-nearest-jobcentre.dwp.gov.uk/

entries.title: Travel or clothing when starting work
entries.description:
The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help with travel to a new job. A Jobcentre work coach may consider the Flexible Support Fund. Apply before paying when possible; neither is automatic.
Manchester emergency support options

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Shelter Greater Manchester
entries.description:
New Legal Aid appointments: 0344 515 1774, Monday–Friday 9am–4pm. An appointment and eligibility check are required.
National emergency housing helpline: 0808 800 4444, Monday–Friday 8am–5pm.
Shelter Greater Manchester
entries.address: Main office: Unit 3, Great Northern Tower, 5 Watson Street, Manchester M3 4EE

entries.title: Greater Manchester Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 769 2244; email: reception@gmlaw.org.uk. Housing appointments are normally Monday–Friday 9am–5pm; leave a name and number. — mailto:reception@gmlaw.org.uk
Free advice and representation for people homeless or at risk in Greater Manchester, including eligible Legal Aid housing and public-law cases.
Law Centre housing help
entries.address: Address: 669 Stockport Road, Longsight, Manchester M12 4QE

entries.title: Citizens Advice Manchester
entries.description:
Call 0808 278 7800 for free advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment, care, family crisis and some immigration issues.
Citizens Advice contact

entries.title: Housing Possession Court Duty Scheme
entries.description:
Free on-the-day advice and representation is available to defendants regardless of income. Contact Shelter Manchester on 0344 515 1711 or manchesterdutyscheme@shelter.org.uk. — mailto:manchesterdutyscheme@shelter.org.uk
Take court papers, tenancy, rent statement and messages. Do not miss the hearing while waiting for advice.
Manchester housing-duty information

entries.title: Civil Legal Advice
entries.description:
Call 0345 345 4345. Legal Aid advice may be available for eligible housing, debt, discrimination and domestic-abuse problems.
Civil Legal Advice

entries.title: National Insurance number
entries.description:
Check old payslips, benefit letters or a tax account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work.
Apply for a National Insurance number

entries.title: Prove the right to work
entries.description:
Some people use a share code; others use original documents. Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Citizens Advice or GMIAU if your status is unclear.
Official right-to-work service

entries.title: Replace a birth certificate
entries.description:
Order through the General Register Office or relevant local register office. Fees apply. Ask a support worker about safe delivery or fee help.
Order a certificate

entries.title: Passport advice
entries.description:
Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or a delivery address are difficult. Charities cannot guarantee fees.
Passport Adviceline

entries.title: Bank account and benefit payments
entries.description:
Ask about a basic bank account and acceptable alternative ID. Never let another person control your benefit card, PIN or online account.
MoneyHelper basic bank accounts

entries.title: Phone and online access
entries.description:
Libraries provide free Wi-Fi. Day centres may help with calls and forms. The Cost of Living Advice Line can assess possible help with data, a phone, laptop or internet; devices are not guaranteed.
Cost of Living Advice Line

entries.title: Mail and document storage
entries.description:
Ask whether a hostel, day centre or Jobcentre can authorise a care-of address and secure document storage. Confirm collection deadlines.
Do not send post or leave papers or belongings at a service without explicit permission. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found.
Official care-of address options

entries.title: Greater Manchester Immigration Aid Unit
entries.description:
Free immigration and asylum legal advice is requested through an online referral, normally open Monday–Thursday. The office is appointment-only.
If you cannot complete the form, call 0161 740 7722 Friday 12 noon–3pm for form help. This slot does not provide legal advice. General email cannot accept advice referrals.
GMIAU advice referral forms
entries.address: Office: 1 Delaunays Road, Crumpsall, Manchester M8 4QS

entries.title: Boaz Trust Restricted Eligibility Support Service
entries.description:
For non-UK nationals aged 18+ in Greater Manchester who are single or a couple, have restricted eligibility or no recourse to public funds, and are homeless or at risk. Boaz and Booth Centre provide outreach with GMIAU immigration advice.
The online referral is normally reviewed weekly. It is not a same-day accommodation guarantee and is not designed for families.
Boaz referral information

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Call 0808 8010 503, free, for asylum support, destitution, accommodation problems and help finding legal representation. Migrant Help is not a law firm.
GOV.UK asylum helplines

entries.title: Destitute Migrants Relief Fund
entries.description:
Street Support explains the current partner route for a small crisis grant for people with no recourse to public funds. Applications go through participating organisations and are not guaranteed.
Street Support Manchester

entries.title: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
entries.description:
Call 08000 121 700. Current temporary hours are 12 noon–5pm daily. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Confidential guidance if someone is controlled, threatened, forced to work or have sex, has pay or documents withheld, or cannot leave. You do not have to give your name.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: Manchester Women's Aid
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 660 7999, Monday–Friday 10am–1pm; email: referrals@manchesterwomensaid.org. — mailto:referrals@manchesterwomensaid.org
Domestic-abuse safety planning, community help and refuge assessment. A refuge place depends on assessment and vacancies. The free Pankhurst Centre women's drop-in is Wednesday 12 noon–2pm and includes lunch.
National Domestic Abuse Helpline: 0808 2000 247, 24 hours. Call 999 in immediate danger.
Manchester Women's Aid

entries.title: Saheli
entries.description:
Helpline: 0161 945 4187, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm; email: help@saheli.org.uk. — mailto:help@saheli.org.uk
Multilingual, culturally appropriate help concerning domestic abuse, forced marriage and leaving an unsafe situation. The public address is a post box; call rather than travelling.
Saheli help

entries.title: MASH: women who sex work
entries.description:
Freephone: 0800 183 0499. No appointment is needed during published drop-in hours; check the live timetable.
Free, confidential and trans-inclusive help for women who currently or previously sex worked, are considering it or are being forced to do so. Food, computers, condoms, needle exchange, sexual-health nursing, housing, benefits, safety and casework are available.
MASH drop-in
entries.address: Address: 94–96 Fairfield Street, Manchester M1 2WR

entries.title: Centrepoint: ages 16–25
entries.description:
Free helpline: 0808 800 0661, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Manchester accommodation is for ages 18–25 through a council referral.
Under 18, tell the council and Children's Services immediately that you have nowhere safe; call 999 if at immediate risk.
Centrepoint housing helpline

entries.title: akt: LGBTQ+ young people aged 16–25
entries.description:
Young people who are homeless, sofa surfing, at risk or in a hostile home can self-refer, use live chat or email gethelp@akt.org.uk. Chat is normally Monday–Thursday 10am–4:30pm and Friday 10am–3pm. — mailto:gethelp@akt.org.uk
Manchester office phone: 0161 228 3308. The office is appointment-only. Housing access, advice, advocacy and education or employment support may be available; a bed is not guaranteed.
akt immediate support

entries.title: LGBT Foundation
entries.description:
Helpline: 0345 330 3030; email: helpline@lgbt.foundation. — mailto:helpline@lgbt.foundation
Emotional support, sexual health, domestic-abuse, mental-health and recovery support for LGBTQ+ people. It is not emergency accommodation.
Council LGBT Foundation listing
entries.address: Address: Fairbairn House, 2nd Floor, 72 Sackville Street, Manchester M1 3NJ

entries.title: Op FORTITUDE: veterans
entries.description:
Call 0800 952 0774. Veterans homeless or at risk can self-refer for tenancy support or specialist housing. Advice is available, but accommodation is individually assessed and not guaranteed.
GOV.UK veteran homelessness support

entries.title: Age UK Manchester: age 60+
entries.description:
Advice Line: 0161 833 3944, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9am–4:30pm; email: advice@ageukmanchester.org.uk. — mailto:advice@ageukmanchester.org.uk
Free benefits, housing, utilities and social-care advice. Say immediately if you are homeless or facing hospital discharge without safe accommodation.
Age UK Manchester advice

entries.title: Adult social care, disability and safeguarding
entries.description:
Phone: 0161 234 5001; email: mcsreply@manchester.gov.uk. — mailto:mcsreply@manchester.gov.uk
Adults aged 18+ can ask for advice or an assessment when illness, disability, injury, abuse or a major life change affects daily living or safety. Online referrals are not emergencies; phone for an urgent concern.
Social care does not replace a homeless application. Contact both teams if care needs affect safe accommodation.
Manchester adult social care

entries.title: Care leavers
entries.description:
Tell the housing team that you are a care leaver and contact your personal adviser. Manchester's leaving-care service can help with housing, benefits and setting up home.
Care-leaver housing help

entries.title: StreetVet
entries.description:
Free veterinary support for pets belonging to people who meet the legal definition of homelessness. Complete the help form; registration and treatment depend on an eligibility check.
StreetVet is not an emergency service and does not pay existing bills or provide fostering. In an animal emergency, contact a veterinary practice.
StreetVet help form

entries.title: Dogs Trust Together Through Homelessness
entries.description:
Phone: 020 7833 7611, Monday–Friday 10am–4pm; email: tth@dogstrust.org.uk. — mailto:tth@dogstrust.org.uk
The UK-wide scheme can help eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. Assessment and participating providers apply.
Together Through Homelessness

entries.title: Tell every service about your pet
entries.description:
Many placements cannot accept animals; some can. Tell the council and any referrer the species, size, health and vaccination status. Ask for a pet-friendly option before accepting or rejecting a placement.
Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting admission.
Search dog-friendly services
